clips.start_words: Why are Americans the most depressed
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's claim: America has some of the highest depression rates on earth, and he points first at the food.

His example: red dye the FDA itself called too toxic to touch skin in a cosmetic - yet still approved for food.

His list of what he says feeds low mood: aspartame, sucralose and NutraSweet in diet drinks and protein shakes, plus corn syrup solids in ultra-processed food.

His view: genetically modified, heavily processed food can also throw off gut balance, which he ties back to mood.

Comment HEALTH and we'll send you the ingredients to avoid.

#kevintrudeau #readthelabel #guthealth #wbdaily #healthtruth #naturalhealth

Kevin Trudeau's claim: almost everyone he's seen with depression tests low in one mineral - lithium, not the drug, the trace mineral.

His story: when 7-Up launched as 'The Uncola,' it skipped the cocaine Coca-Cola started with and the caffeine from kola nut - and ran on raw cane sugar, carbonation and a small dose of mineral lithium instead, for the same lift.

His point: the pharmaceutical version is a patented, man-made form of the same mineral your body may already be short on.

Comment HEALTH and we'll send you where the real mineral shows up.

Kevin Trudeau's go-to list for a low mood, by his own account.

Lithium orate: a mineral, not the drug, that he says most people are deficient in - it was even the hidden ingredient in the original 7-Up.

St. John's Wort, an herb he calls a fast lift. B vitamins, which he says most people run low on and which steady energy. Guarana, a natural caffeine source without the jitters.

His favorite: a small square of organic raw cacao, 85% dark, nothing but cacao and a little raw cane sugar - what he calls a real mood elevator.

Kevin Trudeau's low-cost pick for stress and low mood: a mini trampoline.

His reasoning: jumping on a rebounder (he credits his friend Al Carter, who wrote a whole book on rebound exercise) stimulates the lymphatic system and squeezes every cell in the body, which he says helps move toxins out.

His backup list if you skip the trampoline: yoga, running, calisthenics, Pilates, martial-arts style stretching, or straightforward strength training - any of it, he says, helps.
